newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police hunt documents in ELF Gabon probe.
newsitem.headline: French police hunt documents in ELF Gabon probe.

text.p: Police searched the offices of France's financial police on Wednesday in a probe into the disappearance of documents linking a Swiss bank account held by Andre Tarallo, chairman of a unit of ELF Aquitaine oil company, with Gabon President Omar Bongo, police sources said.
The documents, which were under seal, disappeared from financial police headquarters earlier this month.
Paris judge Eva Joly had been using them as part of her ultra-sensitive investigation into Elf's activities in the West African state.
Police sources said the IGS police inspection service was searching the whole 13-storey building where the financial police and other services are headquartered.
The Communist CGT union's police branch denounced Wednesday's search as an act casting suspicion over financial police members.
Four financial police officers were detained and questioned by the IGS on Friday. They had been entrusted by Joly with seizing the documents at the home of a Saint-Tropez decorator.

Tarallo, chairman of Elf's Gabon subsidiary, is under judicial investigation in France on suspicion of receiving the proceeds of misuse of corporate funds. He is currently on 10 million francs ($1.8 million) bail.
Judicial sources have said Tarallo told Joly he opened a bank account in Switzerland that was used solely by Bongo.
Joly is investigating suspected fraud at Elf involving the payment of alleged covert commissions while former French railways chief Loic Le Floch-Prigent was chairman from 1988 to 1993.
She placed Le Floch-Prigent in preventive detention last year but he was released in December after six months.
